newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close lower as recovery falters.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close lower as recovery falters.

text.p: Tokyo stocks turned tail after a morning rally and closed lower on Tuesday, with shares of leading blue-chip companies weighed down by persistent worries over Japan's feeble economic recovery, brokers said.
Wall Street's rebound on Monday initially helped the key Tokyo index to recover, but buying later fizzled.
The 225-share Nikkei average shed 80.10 points or 0.42 percent to end at 18,961.00. Nikkei September futures slipped 70 points to 18,930.
"We've confirmed a lack of recovery power," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Brokers said high-priced shares of technology companies, especially Sony Corp, were hit by profit-taking in the afternoon and that dragged down the key Nikkei index.
"Behind the index's recovery is fragile, there is a feeling that the economy remains weak," Karikomi said.
In the long-term interest rate market, the yield of the key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) fell to 2.060 percent early on Tuesday, a record low for any benchmark 10-year JGB.
On the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE), turnover was 342 million shares.
The volume compared to 360 million shares on Monday.
Advancing issues outpaced decliners 566 to 482, while 199 issues were unchanged.
The TOPIX index of all first-section stocks dipped 7.29 points or 0.49 percent to 1,483.00.
The Nikkei 300 retreated 1.90 point or 0.65 percent to end at 289.92.

Analysts expected the Tokyo stock market to remain under downward pressure. But many said the key Nikkei 225 index was likely to be supported at 18,300 to 18,500, as Japan's economy is still on a recovery trend.

"What hurts the economy is weak consumer spending, which is a temporary factor. The basic scenario of a mild economic recovery in Japan is unchanged," said Tamizo Kimura, chief strategist at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics Inc.
Among leading blue-chip shares, electronics giant Sony slipped on profit-taking, hurting overall sentiment, brokers said. Its share price fell 500 yen to close at 11,000.
Shares of firms making equipment to produce semiconductors also retreated on profit-taking. Tokyo Electron Ltd was down 240 yen at 7,410.
Also, Canon Inc was down 140 yen at 3,560 and Advantest Corp fell 500 yen at 11,800.
Blue-chip shares in general gained ground in the morning on U.S. stocks' recovery on Monday.
On Monday, the Dow jumped 109 points to 7,803, a gain of 1.4 percent. The U.S. blue-chips' index posted its second-largest point loss ever on Friday, jarring Tokyo stocks on Monday.
By sector, gainers were led by sea transport, mining, textile, railway/bus and foods. The major losers were electric equipment, automobiles and transport equipment.

After the market closed on Tuesday, private research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd said medium-sized contractor Daito Kogyo Co Ltd had applied for court protection from creditors under Japanese bankruptcy laws with debts of 154.4 billion yen.
Daito Kogyo said it would hold a news conference regarding the application at 6.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
The second section index closed 1.06 point lower at 1,662.02, with 6.14 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 3.31 points at 1,061.78.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk (81-3-3714-5473)
